label: Born at Vik, near Uppsala
description: Svante August Arrhenius was born on 19 February 1859.

sources.quote: The Swedish chemist and physicist Svante August Arrhenius was born on 19 February 1859 at Vik, near Uppsala

label: Died in Stockholm
description: Arrhenius died on 2 October 1927 in Stockholm at the age of 67.

sources.quote: and he died on 2 October 1927 in Stockholm.
shortly before his death in 1927, at the age of 67.

label: Undergraduate studies at University of Uppsala
description: Arrhenius completed undergraduate studies at the University of Uppsala before 1881.

sources.quote: After undergraduate studies at the University of Uppsala, in 1881 Arrhenius went to Stockholm College

label: Moved to Stockholm College
description: Arrhenius went to Stockholm College to prepare for his doctoral dissertation.

sources.quote: in 1881 Arrhenius went to Stockholm College (Högskola) to prepare for his doctoral dissertation in Uppsala

label: Doctoral dissertation on electrical conductivity
description: Arrhenius completed his dissertation investigating the electrical conductivity of electrolytes and introduced the ionic theory of dissociation.

sources.quote: While in Stockholm, Arrhenius investigated the electrical conductivity of electrolytes, which was an important part of his dissertation of 1884.

label: Received travel grant from Royal Swedish Academy
description: Arrhenius received a travel grant which he used for extensive studies abroad.

sources.quote: In 1886 Arrhenius received a travel grant from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

label: Appointed lecturer at Stockholm College
description: Arrhenius was appointed lecturer at Stockholm College.

sources.quote: In 1891 he was appointed lecturer at Stockholm College

label: Established Physics Society
description: Arrhenius took the initiative to establish a Physics Society with the aim of offering lectures and promoting discussions.

sources.quote: The same year that Arrhenius started in his position as physics lecturer at Stockholm College, he took the initiative to establish a Physics Society (Fysiska Sällskapet)

label: Promoted to professor of physics
description: Arrhenius was promoted to professor of physics at Stockholm College.

sources.quote: and promoted four years later to professor of physics.

label: Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry
description: Arrhenius earned a Nobel Prize in chemistry for his ionic theory of dissociation.

sources.quote: which turned out to be of such importance that it earned him a Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1903.

label: Published Lehrbuch der kosmischen Physik
description: Arrhenius published a massive treatise on cosmical physics in two volumes.

sources.quote: Lehrbuch der kosmischen Physik that he published in 1903

label: Lectured at Congress of Arts and Science in St. Louis
description: Arrhenius gave a much publicized lecture in the section of cosmical physics.

sources.quote: He was one of the European luminaries invited to the 1904 Congress of Arts and Science in St. Louis, where he gave a much publicized lecture

label: Became director of Nobel Institute for Physical Chemistry
description: Arrhenius became the first director of the Nobel Institute for Physical Chemistry.

sources.quote: In 1905 he became the first director of the Nobel Institute for Physical Chemistry under the Royal Swedish Academy

label: Published Worlds in the Making
description: Arrhenius presented qualitative cosmological theory in his best-selling book, translation of a Swedish book from 1907.

sources.quote: Worlds in the Making, a translation of a Swedish book from 1907

label: Joined Nobel Committee for Physics
description: Arrhenius had been a member of the Nobel Committee for Physics since its beginning in 1900.

sources.quote: Arrhenius, who had been a member of the Nobel Committee for Physics since its beginning in 1900.
